Kimberly,

Thanks for sending the draft — attached are our redlines for the MSA and Order Form. High level: procurement/legal are ok with most commercial items but we're pushing back on the auto-renew and termination-for-convenience mechanics.

Key asks from Aperio:
- Increase notice window for non-renewal to 90 days (from proposed 60). With our fiscal planning we need additional runway to re-procure and schedule migration.
- Termination for convenience should include a 90-day notice and a cap equal to 6 weeks of average monthly usage to make potential churn less disruptive for our customers.
- For enterprise deals (>$1M ARR) we may require a minimum transition assistance SLA (data export & hands-on support) in the contract.

We prefer tracked changes in the attached PDF. Can your legal team review and propose firm alternative language? If helpful, I'm available for a 30-minute call Thursday morning PT.

Maria — thanks for the quick turnaround and the clear note. Appreciate the context on fiscal planning. I've pulled in our legal and sales ops for a quick review.

Short response / proposal:
- Standard Redwood position is 60 days' notice for non-renewal. That balances SKU scheduling and capacity planning across Dedicated customers.
- We're open to a one-off concession for enterprise deals to extend to 90 days provided there is either: (a) a 12-month firm term extension OR (b) an agreed transition assistance package (we can document the level of hands-on support).
- For Termination for Convenience (TFC), we generally cap exposure at 3 months of committed fees (or remaining committed spend, whichever is lower) rather than a weeks-based cap. This aligns with our revenue recognition and enables predictable ramp-down.

If that sounds reasonable, I'll ask Legal to draft specific clause language we can insert directly into your tracked PDF. Happy to take the 30-min call on Thursday; propose 9:00am PT.

Kim / Ben — reviewed Aperio's redlines. My high-level take and proposed concrete language below.

1) Notice window (auto-renew):
- Position: standard 60 days for non-renewal.
- Enterprise concession: agree to 90 days if customer commits to a minimum 12-month renewal term (i.e., a multiyear or 12-month extension at signature).

Suggested clause (MSA §2.2):
"""
Either party may elect not to renew the then-current Term by providing written notice at least sixty (60) days prior to the end of the then-current Term. For agreements with an Annual Contract Value greater than One Million USD (USD 1,000,000), the notice period shall be ninety (90) days if the Customer elects to enter into a minimum twelve (12) month renewal at the time the renewal is agreed.
"""

2) Termination for Convenience (TFC):
- Risk mitigation: cap as three (3) months of the Customer's then-current committed recurring fees or the remainder of the then-current Term, whichever is less. Avoid weeks-based caps — they are ambiguous with variable usage.

Suggested clause (MSA §8.3):
"""
Either party may terminate this Agreement for convenience upon ninety (90) days' prior written notice. In the event of termination for convenience by Customer, Customer shall pay to Redwood an amount equal to the lesser of (a) three (3) months of Customer's then-current committed recurring fees, or (b) the remaining unpaid portion of the committed fees for the then-current Term.
"""

3) Transition Assistance / Data Export:
- Agree to include a transition assistance commitment for enterprise deals: basic data export plus up to 4 weeks of technical transition support included for accounts > $1M ARR. For smaller deals, offer transition assistance as a billable service.

I can insert the above language into the tracked PDF and send to Maria as a redline. Ben — please confirm whether ops can commit to the 4-week support baseline for enterprise and an estimate of effort/cost.

Maria — appreciate the patience while we reviewed internally. Attached are two items: (1) Redwood counter redlines (tracked) and (2) a short snippet with the proposed clause language we would like to insert (redwood-term-snippet-20270330.txt).

Summary of our proposed compromise: 
- Notice window: Standard 60 days' notice for non-renewal. For enterprise deals (ACV > $1,000,000) Redwood will accept 90 days if Aperio simultaneously agrees to a minimum 12-month renewal term upon renewal signature.
- Termination for Convenience: Customer may terminate for convenience with 90 days' notice. Customer liability is capped at the lesser of (a) three (3) months of committed recurring fees, or (b) the remaining committed fees for the then-current Term.
- Transition assistance: For enterprise deals Redwood will include basic data export and up to four (4) weeks of technical transition support at no additional charge. For smaller accounts, transition assistance is available as a paid service (we're happy to provide an SOW).

Next steps:
- If this is acceptable, confirm in writing and we'll prepare an updated Order Form and DocuSign envelope.
- If Aperio prefers the 90-day notice without a 12-month renewal commitment, we'll need to propose a commercial offset (e.g., a modest price uplift or a transition fee) — happy to discuss in the call.

Proposed meeting: Thu 9:00am PT to walk redlines and finalize. Please confirm.
